PROPOSED NOTICE FOR THE PARTIAL IPA POSITIVE-EVIDENCE DATA

Scope of this notice
The IPA-derived positive ledger, its runtime data representation, and their
generated data equivalents are separately licensed data. The project's MIT
license for independently authored implementation code does not replace these
data licenses. This proposal contains no chart artwork, PDF, font, or outline.

Changes and adapted-data license
This project selected an explicitly partial set of symbols and literal examples
from the visually reviewed 2015 chart, cross-referenced selected encodings using
the 2026 mapping aid, added Unicode 13 identities and explicit canonical
equivalence records, and expressed the results in an auditable data ledger.
The chart layout, typography, artwork, and fonts are not reproduced in this data.
The resulting IPA-derived adapted data is offered under CC-BY-SA-4.0, preserving
the original source notices above. ShareAlike applies to covered adaptations of
the data. Nothing here restricts uses that applicable law already permits.
There is no endorsement by the International Phonetic Association, Unicode,
SIL International, or any font creator. Preserve required attribution, change
indications, license links, and warranty disclaimers when redistributing.
The licensed material is offered without warranties as described in the linked
licenses. This dataset is PARTIAL and is not a complete IPA repertoire,
transcription grammar, or pronunciation-correctness validator.

DerivedAge copyright: © 2019 Unicode, Inc.
https://www.unicode.org/Public/13.0.0/ucd/UnicodeData.txt
https://www.unicode.org/Public/13.0.0/ucd/DerivedAge.txt
Unicode-derived fields retain the separate Unicode copyright and permission
notice in LICENSE-UNICODE-V3.txt. That notice is the preserved current
1991–2026 license snapshot, not a claim about a historical 2020 license text.
https://www.unicode.org/license.txt

Detailed source pins, row provenance, limitations, and modifications accompany
the data in the positive ledger and manifest. The original text being assessed
is never rewritten by these records; no compatibility normalization is applied.
